A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same step-entropy CoT compression work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite retitling, reorganization and substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning, SFT/GRPO and reward-ablation experiments, plus mathematical and MMLU evaluations in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds numerical comparisons with external compression methods and a pruning-placeholder ablation.

M1.justification: v2 introduces length-normalized step entropy, averaging token entropies to address the length bias of v1's summed score. The pruning and SFT/GRPO framework remains intact. Section 3.2 still instructs using the summed score in Equation 2, leaving unclear which variant underlies the reported experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepScaleR and OpenR1-Math, evaluate GSM8k, Math500 and AIME2024/2025, and include MMLU College Medicine and High School History in their appendices. The added comparisons and placeholder ablation reuse existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds evaluated comparisons with Token-efficient Prompts, LC-Prompt, CoT-Valve, TokenSkip and R1-Compress on Math500 and AIME2024. Token-efficient Prompts corresponds to Prompt-BeConcise in Appendix D. Their source papers were already cited, but v1 contained no corresponding numerical comparisons.

E3.justification: The mathematical-result tables switch from total thinking tokens to averages per answer, and new Table 4 reports changes relative to Full-CoT. Appendix E adds a controlled replacement-strategy evaluation at 80%, 85% and 90% pruning on the existing 50-sample DeepScaleR setting. Existing training budgets and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E and Figure 4 add a focused ablation comparing [SKIP], [MASK], 'and then' and direct deletion, testing whether replacement choice preserves accuracy under aggressive pruning. The reward-component ablation, step-versus-token analysis and model/domain analyses already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added comparisons and ablation continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds external-comparator results in Table 4 and replacement-strategy results in Figure 4. Table 1 revises the DeepSeek-R1-7B GSM8k baseline from 80.36% to 78.54%, and its pruning token saving from 0.6% to 1.3%. New Figure 4 reports [SKIP] accuracy of 72%/70% at 85%/90% pruning, whereas retained Figure 1 shows 68%/72% under the same stated model and sampled data.

T1.justification: v2 adds the formal length-normalized entropy definition in Equation 3 and corrects the subset cardinality to K+1. The mutual-information bounds and their derivations already appeared in v1; labeling them Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 and moving their proofs to Appendix B does not constitute new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central step-entropy, 80% pruning and autonomous SFT/GRPO compression claims. Section 4.3 nevertheless adds an explicit claim of a new state-of-the-art accuracy-efficiency trade-off and outperforming existing compression methods, extending v1's narrower effectiveness claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of placeholder benefits and learned versus static pruning. Its limitations now identify sensitivity to newline-based segmentation and distinguish existing mathematical/MMLU validation from untested open-ended and multimodal reasoning. The original redundancy interpretation and concern about a universally fixed pruning threshold remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D supplies exact prompting-baseline instructions, and Figure 3 newly identifies DeepSeek-R1-14B and DeepScaleR for the retained step-versus-token experiment. A new reproducibility statement lists planned code/configuration releases, although both abstracts say code and data are already released. The PDFs therefore do not establish a change in actual availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Hendrycks et al. MMLU reference and expands positioning through baseline descriptions and explicit superiority claims in Section 4.3 and Appendix D. The related-work discussion and its distinction between step compression, token compression and latent reasoning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: two-stage training moves into the method section, proofs and reward ablations move into dedicated appendices, and training analysis and conclusion/limitations are rewritten. It introduces lettered appendices, ethics and reproducibility statements, and updates the title and affiliation text.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column conference formatting. v1 Figures 2 and 3 become Figure 2 panels, a comparison table and placeholder-ablation plot are added, and existing tables are resized and reformatted with average-token headings and colored reductions. Figure 1's plotted image is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful external comparisons, a placeholder ablation and clearer segmentation/domain limitations. However, the new normalized entropy definition is not reconciled with the algorithm's summed-entropy instruction, and new Figure 4 conflicts with retained Figure 1 at matching pruning ratios under the same stated setup. These ambiguities affect the interpretation and credibility of the added evidence, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
